definition: Six Little Dragons (Chinese: 杭州六小龙), or Six Little Dragons of Hangzhou, are an informal grouping of the tech startups Game Science, DeepSeek, Unitree Robotics, DEEP Robotics, BrainCo and Manycore Tech.
details: All six were established in Hangzhou. They are active in tech fields such as artificial intelligence, robotics, gaming, and brain-computer interface technology. Hangzhou is referred to as the China's "e-commerce capital" (电商之都). The nickname "Six Little Dragons" originated from the Chinese internet.

explainer.lead: Six Little Dragons (Chinese: 杭州六小龙) is an informal grouping of six Hangzhou tech startups: Game Science, DeepSeek, Unitree Robotics, DEEP Robotics, BrainCo and Manycore Tech. It matters as a shorthand for a cluster of firms working across AI, robotics, gaming and brain-computer interfaces in China's e-commerce capital.

tiers.eli5: Think of it as a nickname the Chinese internet gave to six ambitious tech companies that all grew up in the same city, Hangzhou. Between them they make games, AI models, robots and brain-computer tech.
tiers.practitioner: The term is useful as shorthand when mapping China's AI and robotics startup landscape, since all six were established in Hangzhou. A pitfall is treating it as a formal category: it is an informal nickname that originated on the Chinese internet, not an industry classification.
tiers.paperLevel: An informal grouping rather than a technical definition; membership is fixed at Game Science, DeepSeek, Unitree Robotics, DEEP Robotics, BrainCo and Manycore Tech, all established in Hangzhou, and the nickname has no formal criteria or ranking behind it.

explainer.example: A market overview of Hangzhou's tech scene lists DeepSeek and Unitree Robotics alongside the other four firms under the Six Little Dragons label to show the city's spread across AI, robotics and gaming.
